dedupe_keys.name: data for replication of the publication probabilistic leak localization in water distribution networks using a hybrid data driven and model based approach

description: Ganjour Mazaev and colleagues publish field-experiment data used to evaluate probabilistic leak localisation in operational drinking-water networks. The study compares an uncalibrated hydraulic model with an extended network whose large areas are relatively insensitive to leaks. Simulated pressure heads train the predictor, while historical measurements support a changing bias correction. The October 2022 deposit provides data.zip free under CC BY 4.0. Public metadata leave the site geography, measurement dates, sampling interval, number of leak events and internal schema unknown. These observations can test whether hydraulic simulations and location estimates remain useful under model bias or weak pressure signals. The reported uncertainty increases where leaks do not cause detectable pressure drops. A separate Zenodo deposit contains the corresponding research code, recorded separately in this review. No related catalogue record is explicitly identified; the archive was not opened.
